create.name: Rebecca Bradshaw
create.bio:
Rebecca Bradshaw has practised vipassana since 1983, in the United States and in Myanmar, and began teaching in 1993 after training at the Insight Meditation Society. Her root lineage is the Mahasi method from Burma; her first teachers were Sayadaw U Pandita, Joseph Goldstein and Sharon Salzberg, and above all from Michele McDonald. Later she studied the Thai Forest tradition and the Kwan Yin practices of the Chan lineage with Kittisaro and Thanissara. She is now Guiding Teacher Emeritus of IMS and of Pioneer Valley's Insight Meditation Center in Easthampton, Massachusetts, and holds a master's degree in counselling psychology.

Her teaching is earthy and body-based, coloured by years of qi gong and by plenty of lovingkindness, and she often brings the woods, water and animals into her talks. For many years she has been part of the IMS three-month retreat team, has taught retreats for young adults, and has led retreats in Spanish. Her book Down to Earth Dharma (Shambhala, 2024) looks at the Buddha's teaching through what she calls a receptive or feminine paradigm, balancing an inherited emphasis on effort and striving. She teaches residential retreats at IMS and the Forest Refuge and at centres in Minnesota, Ohio and New York, gives online talks, and has around 250 recorded talks on Dharma Seed.

books.title: Down to Earth Dharma: Insight Meditation to Awaken the Heart
books.author: Rebecca Bradshaw
books.description: Her first book, published by Shambhala in 2024 and arranged in four parts: mindfulness, the heart, wisdom and engagement. Drawing on Theravada teaching, nature and personal stories, it invites readers to balance active striving with receptivity, feeling and a sense of belonging to the earth.

courses.title: March at the Forest Refuge (2027)
courses.description: A month of silent practice at the Forest Refuge, the IMS centre for longer retreats in Barre, co-taught with Devin Berry. Retreatants can come for the whole month or stay at least a week, working with insight or lovingkindness practice.
courses.price: From $115 USD per night (IMS 2027 sliding scale, minimum 7 nights)

courses.title: Vipassana and Loving Kindness Retreat at the Insight Meditation Society (April 2027)
courses.description: A week-long silent residential retreat at the IMS Retreat Center in Barre with Roxanne Dault and Greg Scharf, combining insight meditation with lovingkindness. Booking is through IMS.

courses.title: Disentangling the Tangle: Half-Day Retreat at New York Insight
courses.description: A three-hour workshop with New York Insight on using mindfulness and compassion to loosen old, habitual stories about ourselves, such as never being good enough. She works through five stages of relating to these patterns.

courses.title: Twin Cities Vipassana Collective Annual Winter Retreat
courses.description: A week-long winter retreat in Minnesota for the Twin Cities Vipassana Collective, co-taught with Chas DiCapua.

courses.title: Vipassana and Loving Kindness Retreats in Ohio
courses.description: Residential retreats in Milford, Ohio, hosted by the Yellow Springs Dharma Center and co-taught with Candace Cassin and Robert Pryor. Participants can choose a weekend, a week or the full nine days.

free_resources.title: Rebecca Bradshaw's Dharma Talks on Dharma Seed
free_resources.description: Around 250 recorded talks and guided meditations from her retreats, free to stream or download.

Hub programmes are linked through the event pages on her own site, not dharma.org: the Forest Refuge 2027 schedule page is already the IMS hub listing's offering URL (ingest would skip it) and has no page per month, and the April 2027 Retreat Center retreat is only on events.dharma.org, which may not be fetched.
Prices for the April IMS retreat and her non-IMS retreats are not on the pages read, so they say 'Contact for pricing'.
Co-teaches March 2027 at the Forest Refuge with Devin Berry (rank 1); same month appears on both plans with different URLs.
Holds a counselling psychology master's and the IMS page says she is a Licensed Mental Health Counselor; her teaching is dharma, not therapy, so this was left out of the bio.
